title: The Rhythm Club and who jammed
summary: Greer says the Rhythm Club was a social club; he didn't jam; Jabbo Smith never played with the band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When you all were there -- I was just reading a book by Rex Stewart* in which he said that because he-- when you guys were first working in the Cotton Club that the

guys, a lot of the guys in Harlem, because it was a segregated club, they didn't think a lot of the band, but different members of the band starting coming out and playing at different places like the Rhythm Club and others.

That was just a hangout. The Rhythm Club was where the guys, like I told you, they'd have different jam sessions and it was a place to hang out after you would get through work, a lot of guys would come in there and sit down and jam.

That's why they called it the Rhythm Club, went down there to play cards, or play pool, they had nice food, that's the Rhythm Club, it wasn't a regular cabaret or nothing like that. It was just like a social club for the musicians. It got so popular. But the guys would go down and if they feel like playing, they'd play. Wasn't no obligation. If the guy feel like he wanted to play something, you know, sit in and jam, go ahead and jam. Everybody went.
Did you go down there and jam much?

Me. After I got through work, I didn't jam nothing. I didn't put no jam on bread. I didn't jam nothing. What you talking about. If they'd pay me, I was for the almighty, a guy ask come on play something, you want to play something. I'd say no, I'll play some pool. I don't want to play no jam. It's all right. I never really went in for that jamming. I was playing for the almighty. Jam what.

But a lot of our guys would go down and play. Johnny would go down and play. Toby, all the guys. If they felt like playing, they'd play. Hawk used to go down and all the top. Jabo and all the guys would go down there and play.
Jabbo Smith played with the band for awhile, didn't he?
With us. No, he never played with us. No. He was a good friend of ours, but he never played with us.
